genZNote: Behind C. albicans, this is one of the most frequently isolated Candida species in bloodstream infections — especially in neutropenic and cancer patients.

morphology.shape: Oval budding yeast; forms true hyphae and pseudohyphae
morphology.arrangement: Budding yeast cells with elongated pseudohyphae

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human GI tract, skin, and mucous membranes; also soil and water
habitat.hostAssociation: Can be part of normal human mucosal microbiota in small numbers; opportunistic pathogen in immunocompromised hosts
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Common in hospital environments and on medical devices

microscopy.appearance: Budding yeast with pseudohyphae and true hyphae

culture.colonyMorphology: Smooth, cream colonies; blue-gray to purple on CHROMagar depending on brand

identificationClues: Germ tube negative, unlike C. albicans — a key first-line distinguishing test
One of the leading non-albicans Candida species causing bloodstream infections, especially in neutropenic and hematologic malignancy patients
Forms abundant pseudohyphae and true hyphae, unlike some other non-albicans species
Distinct colored colonies on CHROMagar Candida help distinguish it presumptively from other Candida species

diseases: Candidemia/invasive candidiasis (especially in neutropenic and cancer patients)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous flora overgrowth or nosocomial transmission via hands/devices; not typically person-to-person outside healthcare settings
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the top non-albicans Candida species in candidemia globally, with a strong association with hematologic malignancy and neutropenia
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Germ tube negativity plus CHROMagar color and biochemical/molecular testing distinguish it from C. albicans and other non-albicans species

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Leading non-albicans Candida species in bloodstream infections among neutropenic patients
